# cancho-gpu

> A compiler for typed tile kernels (the .chx language), written in cancho: it checks a program (every tile consumed exactly once, bounds, shapes, the threadgroup budget), refuses a wrong one with a rule tag, and lowers it to CUDA C and Metal. Every emitted text is held byte for byte to a recorded golden (499 cases in CI), and what a kernel computes is held to a float64 reference. It links only libc; its authority report names what it may do (args, stderr, file read and write, heap, stdout) and no network or foreign code. The same kernels run models on a Metal GPU: Qwen3.8-27B behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo (text to image, photo editing), FastWan2.2-TI2V-5B (video from a prompt) and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B (speech to text), and they train a GPT, a CNN and Qwen2.5 (LoRA and full fine-tuning). Alpha. Limits: every speed is one Apple M4 Max, measured by hand; CUDA has run on one NVIDIA L4 only (176 of 188 device cases of an earlier suite agree with the interpreter, none disagrees).

## Use it
- [Quick start](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu#quick-start): build the compiler at the pinned revision, emit a kernel.
- Compiler: `cancho-gpu emit <file.chx> <dir> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu check <file.chx> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu run <file.chx> [name=value ...] [--target T] [--in NAME FILE ...] [--out NAME ...]`, `cancho-gpu gguf <file.gguf> [--sum]`, `cancho-gpu safetensors <file>`, `cancho-gpu tokenize <tokenizer.json|model.gguf> <corpus>`, `cancho-gpu sample <logits.f32> <vocab> <temperature> <top_p> <top_k> <seed>`. A refusal is `error[<rule>]: <message>` on stderr, exit 1; a usage mistake is exit 2.
- Server: `cancho-gpu-serve <ollama store> tests/chx --port 8080 [--api-key K]` answers `POST /v1/chat/completions` (whole or streamed, thinking mode as `reasoning_content`), `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health` from Qwen3.8-27B. One request at a time; tools, images and `n` other than 1 are refused with a 400 that says why (docs/serving.md).
- Media (a Mac with Apple Silicon): `scripts/media image "<prompt>" -o DIR --size WxH --seed N`, `scripts/media edit PHOTO "<instruction>" -o DIR`, `scripts/media video "<prompt>" -o DIR --frames 17 --size 640x352 [--precise]`, `scripts/media transcribe CLIP.wav -o DIR`, `scripts/media doctor`, `scripts/media models` (docs/cli.md). One model a task; any other `--model` is refused.

## Facts that matter when calling it
- Targets: nvidia-ada (CUDA C) and apple-m-series (Metal), each from the file's schedule. amd-cdna3 (HIP, docs/amd.md) is emitted for kernels that do not use `mma`, which are refused `error[lowering]`; that text runs on a CPU emulator at 64 lanes and has never been compiled or run by AMD's tools.
- Text, Qwen3.8-27B (NVFP4, weights read from Ollama's store): 85, 100 and 113 tokens a second on three code requests with the model's own draft head, where Ollama 0.40.17 gave 81, 101 and 112 once warmed; on prose 46 against 57; about 27 without drafting (docs/serving.md 11.6).
- Image, 1024 x 1024, 8 steps: 61 to 65 s; mflux 52 to 55 s on the same machine. The image is 0.16 of 255 from the float64 pipeline (torch's BF16: 4.75) (docs/diffusion.md).
- Video, 17 frames of 640 x 352: about 21 s run in turn with mlx-video's 23.4 to 23.8 s; the pictures were not compared between engines. `--precise` runs the transformer's products with f32 operands, for 2 to 3 s more (docs/diffusion.md).
- Speech to text: the reference's transcript to the letter on its two clips; 16.2 s of speech in 3.0 s from a cold start; a clip over 152 s is refused (docs/audio.md). Speech synthesis is being built; music is not chosen.
- Training sessions (docs/resident.md): parameters, optimiser state and data stay on the GPU. GPT of 59.95 M parameters: 167.8 ms a step against torch MPS's 196.7. Qwen2.5-0.5B LoRA: 889.2 ms and 16.14 GB against float16 autocast's 1,142.0 ms and 27.48 GB. CNN on CIFAR-10: 17.6 ms against torch's 10.6 (slower), 87.4% test accuracy. One run and one seed each.
- Not implemented or not shown: concurrent requests, tools, AMD, Hopper, CUDA beyond one L4 run, any number from a second machine, speech synthesis, music.

## Optional
- [The language](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/chx.md): .chx, defined.
- [Rules](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/rules.md): every refusal and what triggers it.
- [Design](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/design.md): how the compiler is built and what it cost.
- [Serving](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/serving.md): the endpoint, the prefix cache, the drafts, against Ollama.
- [Diffusion](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/diffusion.md): images, edits and video, stage by stage.
- [Audio](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/audio.md): recognition built, speech in progress.
- [The media command](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/cli.md): image, edit, video, transcribe.
- [Sessions and models](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/resident.md): training on the device, every number with its conditions.
- [Device](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/device.md): driving a GPU, and what stays unproven.
- [README](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu#readme): the full list, with the older work the project page leaves out.
- [Issues](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/issues): the open slices.
